title: The Hendrix riff you can play forever and not get bored
why: A thumb-over chord-melody move in the Hendrix tradition — endlessly loopable once it's in the hands.
note: Focus on the thumb fretting the low E so the top voices ring while you embellish underneath.

title: An easy trick for cool fingerstyle blues riffs
why: A repeatable shape that turns a plain blues into a thumb-and-fingers groove you can improvise over.
note: Keep a steady alternating thumb bass while the top moves — that contrast is the whole sound.

title: Funky blues-style rhythm groove
why: Dominant-7 stabs answered by single low notes — a tight call-and-response groove in E.
note: Mute hard with the fretting hand between stabs; the silence is what makes it funky.

title: A funk-blues groove riff in E
why: Mixes dom-7 chords with single low-string notes — an approachable on-ramp into funk rhythm.
note: Lock the strum hand to a steady 16th-note motion and let the fretting hand pick what sounds.

title: Ten easy bluesy riffs for beginners
why: A pocket grab-bag of classic blues moves — learn one a sitting and bank the rest.
note: Pick the one that sounds most like a song you love and drill it slow with a metronome.

title: Play blues in any key with this one riff
why: A movable shape that transposes anywhere — one pattern, twelve keys.
note: Memorise the root on the low E so you can slide the whole shape to any key on the fly.

title: Three blues riffs every guitarist should know
why: Three vocabulary staples that show up across the whole blues canon.
note: Chain them into a 12-bar — riff one over the I, the others over the IV and V.

title: A fingerstyle acoustic funk-blues groove
why: An E7-centred groove that puts funk feel under fingerstyle — percussive and melodic at once.
note: Add a light palm slap on the backbeat to fake a drummer while you play.

title: Three levels of a one-chord funk groove
why: Same vamp, three depths — a clean ladder from simple comp to full funk workout.
note: Start at level one and only move up once the 16th-note strum stays metronome-tight.
